subject: E-Commerce
title: VAT and the EU's iOSS
description: A fast breakdown of VAT and the EU's iOSS for builders.

hook.text: The EU's Import One-Stop Shop (iOSS) collects VAT at checkout for goods under €150. Sellers collect tax upfront.

buildup.text: Before iOSS, buyers received unexpected VAT bills on delivery. They refused packages and demanded refunds.

discovery.text: iOSS means a US seller charges German 19% VAT at checkout and remits it to the EU. No surprise fees on arrival.

twist.text: Sellers outside the EU must register for iOSS or use a fiscal representative. It adds complexity and cost.

climax.text: iOSS solved surprise taxes but shifted the burden to sellers. Compliance is the new cost of selling globally.

punchline.text: No more surprise VAT at the door. iOSS moved the tax from buyers to sellers.

quiz.question: What problem did the EU's iOSS system solve?
options: Buyers receiving unexpected VAT bills on delivery, causing package refusals
